  - **hole → sphere: FIXED 2026-07-23** (jet-informed rung ordering in
    classify.rs). A short cylinder tessellated as a few rings is
    vertex-ambiguous with a sphere (two same-radius rings at heights ±h lie
    exactly on a sphere of radius √(R²+h²)), so simplest-DOF-first wrongly
    committed the sphere. \`region_is_developable\` now uses the jet's
    \`min/max\` principal-curvature ratio (~0 for cylinder/cone, ~1 for sphere)
    to try the conical rung before the sphere rung for developable regions;
    the jet only orders, so a genuine sphere the jet misreads still falls
    through. Fusion \`plate_with_hole\` (9 tests) re-enabled and passing
    (\`--compare\` volume rel diff 1.1e-9, was 10.8%); genuine spheres
    unregressed. **l_bracket FIXED 2026-07-24**: its second hole is a full
    cylindrical band whose area-weighted plane normal cancels to NaN;
    \`PlanarSurface::fit_surface\` returned that NaN plane and the ladder
    VACUOUSLY validated it (\`dist > vtol\` is false for NaN), committing a
    degenerate plane over the cylinder. Now the planar fit rejects a
    non-finite plane so the ladder falls through to the cylinder rung; both
    l_bracket holes are cylinders and it passes \`--compare\`. Still disabled:
    **onshape plate_with_hole (coarse)** faceted its hole into planar strips
    (coarse facet angles read as sharp) so no cylindrical region forms — a
    coarse-mesh angular-tolerance issue.
  - **fillet over-segmentation: FIXED 2026-07-24** (compete.rs). All three
    filleted models (filleted_cylinder/hole_block/pipe, 13 tests) re-enabled
    and passing \`--compare\`. Four competition fixes: (1) **magnitude-ordered
    principal curvatures** — a concave hole wall's dominant curvature is
    negative and lands in \`k2\`, so gating "is this curved?" on \`|k1|\` read the
    wall as flat and skipped every curved candidate (the deep hole fell to
    freeform); now \`a1=max(|k1|,|k2|)\`, \`a2=min(...)\`. (2) **seed-patch
    conditioning** (\`condition_patch\`): a jet-similar patch bleeds a row or
    two across a short cylinder→fillet tangent junction, pulling the fit off
    so the seed fails its own fit; trim fit-outlier patch faces until the seed
    validates. (3) **DOF-aware claim resolution**: a face several surfaces
    explain within vertex tolerance goes to the simplest (cylinder over torus;
    larger torus over a spurious thin junction ring) — absolute best-fit let a
    sub-micron sliver steal a fillet's rows and fragment it. (4) **fat-torus
    rejection** (\`r ≤ 0.7·R\`): an r≈R torus loosely fits a flat cap and wins
    on area (filleted_pipe).
  - **cone/cylinder** (cone_cylinder): FIXED 2026-07-24 as a bonus of the

    Still open: **cone_tangent_planes** — one cone of a tangent-cone chain
    fits as a freeform patch plus a degenerate huge-radius cone; and
    **cone_15x20** whose reference STEP is faceted (59 planes, not analytic),
    so the surface-coverage test cannot match.
  - **degenerate huge-radius analytic fits on coarse meshes: FIXED
    2026-07-24** (\`radius_plausible\` in compete.rs). A large-radius surface is
    locally almost flat, so a nearly-planar patch fits one within vertex
    tolerance while leaving its radius essentially unconstrained — and because
    the bogus fit floods further than the plane it displaces, it wins the area
    contest. On \`part_rounded_cube\` coarse (a 10 mm cube rounded on its 4
    vertical edges: 4 cylinders + 6 planes) each flat side wall grew an
    r ≈ 32.6 cylinder — nearly twice the model's 17.3 mm bounding-box diagonal
    — over the correct plane, reconstructing 0.39 mm off. A surface belonging
    to the model must fit inside it, so a radius past the bounding-box
    diagonal is degenerate by construction; this is the guard
    \`torus_candidate\` already applied to a torus's major radius, extended to
    cylinders/cones (via \`conical_local_radius\`, since a true cone's

167	/// Decompose a tangent-chain region. Returns the committed analytic
168	/// hypotheses (a strict partition after claim resolution) plus the leftover
169	/// faces no hypothesis explained.
170	pub(super) fn compete_region(
171	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
172	    region: &Region,
173	    jet: &[JetField],
174	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
175	    config: &Config,
176	) -> (Vec<CompeteHyp>, Vec<usize>) {
177	    let n = mesh.faces.len();
178	    let debug = config.verbosity >= 3 || std::env::var("BREPPER_DEBUG_COMPETE").is_ok();
179	    let mut in_region = vec![false; n];
180	    for &fi in &region.faces {
181	        in_region[fi] = true;
182	    }
183	
184	    // Region curvature scale: a face reads "flat" when its principal
185	    // curvature radius exceeds a couple of region diameters.
186	    let extent = region_extent(mesh, region);
187	    let flat_eps = if extent > 0.0 { 1.0 / (2.0 * extent) } else { 1e-6 };
188	
189	    // Upper bound on any committed radius of curvature (see \`radius_plausible\`).
190	    let bb_diag = bounding_box_diagonal(&mesh.vertices);
191	
192	    // Seed order: jet-interior-first (ascending curvature mismatch with
193	    // region neighbors), ties by face index for determinism.
194	    let mut seeds = region.faces.clone();
195	    let score: Vec<f64> = (0..n)
196	        .map(|fi| {
197	            if !in_region[fi] {
198	                return f64::INFINITY;
199	            }
200	            neighbor_jet_mismatch(mesh, fi, jet, &in_region)
201	        })
202	        .collect();
203	    seeds.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
204	        score[a]
205	            .partial_cmp(&score[b])
206	            .unwrap()
207	            .then_with(|| a.cmp(&b))
208	    });
209	
210	    let mut claimed = vec![false; n]; // out of the seed pool once claimed
211	    let mut committed: Vec<CompeteHyp> = Vec::new();

422	/// Grow a hypothesis of type \`S\` from \`seed\`: condition an initial fit on a
423	/// jet-similar seed patch, then flood-accept every region face the fit
424	/// validates and refit on the grown support, to a fixpoint. Returns the
425	/// hypothesis, its validated area, and its face list.
426	fn grow<S: SurfaceType>(
427	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
428	    in_region: &[bool],
429	    seed: usize,
430	    jet: &[JetField],
431	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
432	    config: &Config,
433	    min_faces: usize,
434	) -> Option<(S::Hypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
435	    let patch = seed_patch(mesh, in_region, seed, jet);
436	    grow_from::<S>(mesh, in_region, seed, patch, centroids, config, min_faces)
437	}

439	/// The grow loop proper, from an explicit initial fit patch and flood start:
440	/// fit the patch, flood-accept every region face the fit validates, refit on
441	/// the grown support, to a fixpoint. Returns the hypothesis, its validated
442	/// area, and its face list.
443	fn grow_from<S: SurfaceType>(
444	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
445	    in_region: &[bool],
446	    start: usize,
447	    initial: Vec<usize>,
448	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
449	    config: &Config,
450	    min_faces: usize,
451	) -> Option<(S::Hypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
452	    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm * GROW_VTOL_FACTOR;
453	    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
454	
455	    let mut accepted = condition_patch::<S>(mesh, start, initial, centroids, config, vtol, stol, min_faces);
456	    let mut prev = 0usize;
457	    for round in 0..MAX_GROW_ROUNDS {
458	        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &accepted);
459	        let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, &accepted, &verts, config.verbosity)?;
460	        S::determine_convexity(mesh, &accepted, &mut fit);
461	        let comp = flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, start, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
462	        if comp.is_empty() {
463	            return None; // the start face does not lie on its own fit — reject
464	        }
465	        if comp.len() == accepted.len() && round > 0 {
466	            accepted = comp;
467	            break;
468	        }
469	        if comp.len() == prev {
470	            // Oscillating between two sizes — stop at the larger.
471	            if comp.len() >= accepted.len() {
472	                accepted = comp;
473	            }
474	            break;
475	        }
476	        prev = accepted.len();
477	        accepted = comp;
478	    }
479	
480	    // Final fit + validated flood.
481	    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &accepted);
482	    let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, &accepted, &verts, config.verbosity)?;
483	    S::determine_convexity(mesh, &accepted, &mut fit);
484	    let faces = flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, start, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
485	    if faces.len() < min_faces {
486	        return None;
487	    }
488	    let area: f64 = faces.iter().map(|&fi| face_area(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices)).sum();
489	    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &faces);
490	    let hyp = S::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces.clone(), verts, &fit);
491	    Some((hyp, area, faces))
492	}
493	
494	/// A committed torus's minor radius may not exceed this fraction of its major
495	/// radius. Real fillets and bend tubes are slim (r/R ≤ 0.5 across the corpus:
496	/// full donut 0.3, pipe-elbow 0.5, fillets 0.15–0.2); an r ≈ R "fat" torus is
497	/// a bogus fit a flat cap or wall band accepts loosely and then wins on area
498	/// (filleted_pipe: an r/R = 0.82 torus ate an annular end cap).
499	const MAX_TORUS_RADIUS_RATIO: f64 = 0.7;
500	
501	/// Largest distance from a conical hypothesis's own vertices to its axis: the
502	/// radius for a cylinder, the local radius at the patch for a true cone
503	/// (whose \`radius_at_apex\` is 0, so the field alone cannot be tested).
504	fn conical_local_radius(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &ConicalHypothesis) -> f64 {
505	    let a = hyp.axis_direction;
506	    let mut max_r: f64 = 0.0;
507	    for &vi in &hyp.vertices {
508	        let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
509	        let d = [v.x - hyp.apex[0], v.y - hyp.apex[1], v.z - hyp.apex[2]];
510	        let t = d[0] * a[0] + d[1] * a[1] + d[2] * a[2];
511	        let perp = [d[0] - t * a[0], d[1] - t * a[1], d[2] - t * a[2]];
512	        max_r = max_r.max((perp[0] * perp[0] + perp[1] * perp[1] + perp[2] * perp[2]).sqrt());
513	    }
514	    max_r
515	}
516	
517	/// Rejects a degenerate giant-radius cylinder, cone, or sphere. A large-radius
518	/// surface is locally almost flat, so a nearly-planar patch fits one within
519	/// vertex tolerance while leaving its radius essentially unconstrained — and
520	/// because the bogus fit floods further than the plane it displaces, it wins
521	/// the area contest. On \`part_rounded_cube\` coarse (a 10 mm cube rounded on
522	/// its 4 vertical edges: 4 cylinders + 6 planes) each flat side wall grew an
523	/// r ≈ 32.6 cylinder — nearly twice the model's 17.3 mm bounding-box diagonal
524	/// — over the correct plane, reconstructing 0.39 mm off.
525	///
526	/// A surface belonging to the model must fit inside it, so a radius past the
527	/// bounding-box diagonal is degenerate by construction. This is the same guard
528	/// \`torus_candidate\` already applies to a torus's major radius, extended to the
529	/// other analytic types.
530	///
531	/// Note this is a *validation* fix, not a tolerance one: loosening
532	/// \`--vertex-tolerance\` makes the reconstruction worse (0.39 mm at 1e-1,
533	/// 1.79 mm at 5e-1), because a looser bar admits still more degenerate fits.
534	fn radius_plausible(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &CompeteHyp, bb_diag: f64) -> bool {
535	    hyp_radius(mesh, hyp) <= bb_diag
536	}

538	/// The radius of curvature \`radius_plausible\` bounds. Planes are flat and tori
539	/// are guarded in \`torus_candidate\`, so both report 0 (always plausible).

792	/// Condition the seed patch so the seed lies on the patch's own fit. A

796	/// the wall's toward the fillet's — which pulls the fit off far enough that
797	/// the seed fails its own fit and the grow gives up (leaving the wall to be
798	/// eaten by an over-grown torus). Trim the worst-fitting patch face (never the
799	/// seed) and refit until the seed validates, bottoming out at a size floor so
800	/// the fit stays well-determined. Fit-validated, in the spirit of "validation
801	/// decides geometry"; a no-op when the patch is already clean.
802	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
803	fn condition_patch<S: SurfaceType>(
804	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
805	    seed: usize,
806	    mut patch: Vec<usize>,
807	    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
808	    config: &Config,
809	    vtol: f64,
810	    stol: f64,
811	    min_faces: usize,
812	) -> Vec<usize> {
813	    let floor = min_faces.max(MIN_CONDITION_FACES);
814	    for _ in 0..PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS {
815	        if patch.len() <= floor {
816	            break;
817	        }
818	        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &patch);
819	        let mut fit = match S::fit_surface(mesh, &patch, &verts, config.verbosity) {
820	            Some(f) => f,
821	            None => break,
822	        };
823	        S::determine_convexity(mesh, &patch, &mut fit);
824	        if face_validates::<S>(mesh, seed, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol) {
825	            break;
826	        }
827	        let worst = patch
828	            .iter()
829	            .copied()
830	            .filter(|&f| f != seed)
831	            .max_by(|&a, &b| {
832	                face_max_vertex_dist::<S>(mesh, a, &fit)
833	                    .partial_cmp(&face_max_vertex_dist::<S>(mesh, b, &fit))
834	                    .unwrap()
835	            });
836	        match worst {
837	            Some(w) => patch.retain(|&f| f != w),
838	            None => break,
839	        }
840	    }
841	    patch
842	}

844	/// A small jet-similar patch around \`seed\` (same curvature class, magnitude
845	/// within 2×), capped, for a well-conditioned initial fit.
846	fn seed_patch(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, in_region: &[bool], seed: usize, jet: &[JetField]) -> Vec<usize> {
847	    let seed_class = curvature_class(jet[seed]);
848	    let seed_mag = jet[seed].k1.abs().max(jet[seed].k2.abs());
849	    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
850	    seen.insert(seed);
851	    let mut out = vec![seed];
852	    // Depth-limited BFS (frontier by ring).
853	    let mut frontier = vec![seed];
854	    for _depth in 0..MAX_PATCH_DEPTH {
855	        if out.len() >= SEED_PATCH_CAP {
856	            break;
857	        }
858	        let mut next = Vec::new();
859	        for &fi in &frontier {
860	            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
861	            for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
862	                if ni < 0 {
863	                    continue;
864	                }
865	                let ni = ni as usize;
866	                if !in_region[ni] || seen.contains(&ni) {
867	                    continue;
868	                }
869	                if curvature_class(jet[ni]) != seed_class {
870	                    continue;
871	                }
872	                let mag = jet[ni].k1.abs().max(jet[ni].k2.abs());
873	                if seed_mag > 1e-9 && (mag > 1.5 * seed_mag || mag < 0.667 * seed_mag) {
874	                    continue;
875	                }
876	                seen.insert(ni);
877	                out.push(ni);
878	                next.push(ni);
879	                if out.len() >= SEED_PATCH_CAP {
880	                    break;
881	                }
882	            }
883	        }
884	        frontier = next;
885	    }
886	    out.sort_unstable();
887	    out
888	}

13	//! - **Per seed**: grow each candidate surface type (jet-pruned) from a
14	//!   small jet-similar seed patch — fit, flood-accept every region face the
15	//!   fit validates, refit on the grown support, to a fixpoint — and commit
16	//!   the hypothesis with the **largest validated area** (simplest-DOF

/// TEMP probe: fit `S` to a face set and report the worst vertex distance.
fn probe_fit<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    faces: &[usize],
    verts: &[usize],
    config: &Config,
) -> Option<f64> {
    let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, faces, verts, 0)?;
    S::determine_convexity(mesh, faces, &mut fit);
    let _ = config;
    let mut worst = 0.0_f64;
    for &vi in verts {
        let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
        worst = worst.max(S::vertex_distance(&fit, &[v.x, v.y, v.z]));
    }
    Some(worst)
}

/// Determine convexity: does the face normal point away from the axis (convex) or toward it (concave)?
```

**After:**
```
/// How far a facet normal may stray from the cone's exact normal-axis
/// invariant (`|n·axis| = sin(half_angle)`) before it is judged not to lie on
/// the fit. Tessellation rotates facet normals *around* the axis, which
/// preserves the dot product exactly, so the slack only absorbs chordal sag.
const NORMAL_AXIS_TOL: f64 = 0.05;

/// Does the facet normal field agree with a cone/cylinder of this axis and
/// half-angle? On a cone every facet normal satisfies `|n·axis| =
/// sin(half_angle)`, so the normals pin the axis independently of the vertex
/// positions.
///
/// This is the acceptance test for a fit, not just for a candidate face: on a
/// support that is thin in the axial direction — a one-quad-tall cylinder band
/// between two fillet tori, common in a dense fillet network — the vertex
/// residual barely constrains the axis, and a least-squares cone will happily
/// tip its axis into the band's own plane and beat the true cylinder on
/// residual (measured on `stepped_block_toroidal_fillets`: a bogus 12.2°
/// cone at 3.8e-7 mm against the correct r = 0.5 cylinder at 3.9e-6 mm, with
/// the cone's axis nearly *anti-parallel* to the facet normals). The normals
/// are unambiguous where the positions are degenerate, so they decide.
///
/// Judged on the median face so a few noisy facets cannot veto a real fit;
/// individual offenders are still filtered by `convexity_check` during growth.
fn axis_normals_consistent(
    face_list: &[usize],
    faces: &[MeshFace],
    axis: &[f64; 3],
    half_angle: f64,
) -> bool {
    let expected = half_angle.sin().abs();
    let mut devs: Vec<f64> = face_list
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|&fi| faces[fi].normal)
        .map(|n| (dot3(&n, axis).abs() - expected).abs())
        .collect();
    if devs.is_empty() {
        return true;
    }
    devs.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
    devs[devs.len() / 2] <= NORMAL_AXIS_TOL
}

/// eaten by an over-grown torus). Trim the worst-fitting patch face (never the
/// seed) and refit until the seed validates, bottoming out at a size floor so
/// the fit stays well-determined. Fit-validated, in the spirit of "validation
/// decides geometry"; a no-op when the patch is already clean.
///
/// When the patch admits no fit of this type at all there is no residual to
/// rank by, so the round instead drops the face geometrically farthest from
/// the seed: a straddling patch is unfittable precisely because its far end
/// sits on another surface, and shrinking toward the seed is the one move that
/// is monotonically local.

/// Distance between two faces' centroids.
fn centroid_gap(centroids: &[[f64; 3]], a: usize, b: usize) -> f64 {
    let (p, q) = (centroids[a], centroids[b]);
    ((p[0] - q[0]).powi(2) + (p[1] - q[1]).powi(2) + (p[2] - q[2]).powi(2)).sqrt()
}

> Looking at the medium blob geometry, I'm analyzing two rows of faces with specific curvature values—the negative secondary curvature indicates an inner corner blend torus rather than a standard one. The fit from seven faces leaves a residual error around 3.3e-2, and the primary curvature translates to a radius of 0.455, which is slightly smaller than the nominal 0.5 due to coarse tessellation effects.
> 
> The core issue is that fitting a seven-degree-of-freedom torus to only about ten faces spanning a 90° corner blend is fundamentally under-determined—the patch is too small and sparse relative to the model's complexity. At medium resolution, a 0.5mm blend radius gets roughly two by five quads, which is marginal for this kind of fitting. I suspect this case may require a more sophisticated approach, like seeding the torus fit from the jet curvature or using a normal-based axis determination similar to what worked for the cone, rather than trying to solve it with the current method.
> 
> Actually, there's a more elegant path forward: using the jet's medial points—the tube centers—to directly constrain the torus. For a torus, the medial point of each face (computed as the centroid minus the normal scaled by the principal curvature) lies on the spine circle of radius R. Fitting a circle to these medial points would determine the axis, center, and R directly, then r follows from the principal curvature. This "medial spine" approach was part of the original contingency plan and might be exactly what this coarse-blend case needs. Let me check the test results first to see what the current state looks like, then decide whether to pursue this direction.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Stage 2.7: NURBS fallback (tests/nurbs models)

fn config_for_compare_stage27(stl_path: &str, step_path: &str) -> config::Config {
    let mut config =
        config::parse_config_from(["brepper", stl_path, "--compare", step_path, "--stage=2", "-q"])
            .unwrap();
    config.load_compare_step().unwrap();
    config
}

/// Count selected surfaces by (planar, bspline); assert nothing else was
/// selected. Assertions are on stage 2.6 *selected* surfaces, per policy.
fn planar_bspline_selection_counts(output: &stage2::Stage2Output) -> (usize, usize) {
    let mut planar = 0;
    let mut bspline = 0;
    for s in &output.selected_surfaces {
        match s {
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Planar(_) => planar += 1,
            stage2::SelectedSurface::BSpline(_) => bspline += 1,
            other => panic!("unexpected selected surface type: {other:?}"),
        }
    }
    (planar, bspline)
}

    let mut on_large = vec![false; mesh.faces.len()];

    let enclosed = |h: &CompeteHyp| {

            let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
            f.neighbors[..f.vertex_count as usize]

                        if face_hyp[fi] != usize::MAX {
                            result.dissolved.insert(face_hyp[fi]);
                        }
                    }
                }
                None => result.residual.extend(single),
            }
            continue;
        }

        // Trust the analytic fits: fit only the leftover freeform. It is one
        // connected piece here, which `build_region` requires — a disconnected
        // face set has no single boundary to parameterize over.
        match fit_or_planarize(mesh, &single, face_region, config) {
            Some(fit) => commit_component_fit(fit, &mut result),
            None => result.residual.extend(single),
        }
    }
    result

**After:**
```
        // Absorb the small analytic islands into the freeform patch when the
        // unexplained area dominates — or when the islands are what holds the
        // leftover freeform together AND every piece they separate is itself a
        // patch-sized run of freeform. Islands cutting one freeform surface into
        // several real patches are the accident this rung exists to undo; that
        // is different from real analytic surfaces (a rounded cube's four fillet
        // cylinders) separated by leftover *slivers*, which must stay committed.
        let absorbed = comp.len() - single.len();
        let parts = leftover_components(mesh, &single);
        let islands_split_a_patch =
            parts.len() > 1 && parts.iter().all(|p| p.len() >= MIN_BSPLINE_FACES);
        if absorbed <= single.len() || islands_split_a_patch {
            match fit_or_planarize(mesh, &comp, face_region, config) {
                Some(fit) => {
                    commit_component_fit(fit, &mut result);
                    for &fi in &comp {
                        if face_hyp[fi] != usize::MAX {
                            result.dissolved.insert(face_hyp[fi]);
                        }
                    }
                }
                None => result.residual.extend(single),
            }
            continue;
        }

        // Trust the analytic fits: fit only the leftover freeform, one piece at
        // a time. `build_region` needs a connected face set — a disconnected one
        // has no single boundary to parameterize over.
        for part in parts {
            if part.len() < MIN_BSPLINE_FACES {
                result.residual.extend(part);
                continue;
            }
            match fit_or_planarize(mesh, &part, face_region, config) {
                Some(fit) => commit_component_fit(fit, &mut result),
                None => result.residual.extend(part),
            }
        }
    }

+/// How far a facet normal may stray from the cone's exact normal-axis
+/// invariant (\`|n·axis| = sin(half_angle)\`) before it is judged not to lie on
+/// the fit. Tessellation rotates facet normals *around* the axis, which
+/// preserves the dot product exactly, so the slack only absorbs chordal sag.
+const NORMAL_AXIS_TOL: f64 = 0.05;
+
+/// Does the facet normal field agree with a cone/cylinder of this axis and
+/// half-angle? On a cone every facet normal satisfies \`|n·axis| =
+/// sin(half_angle)\`, so the normals pin the axis independently of the vertex
+/// positions.
+///
+/// This is the acceptance test for a fit, not just for a candidate face: on a
+/// support that is thin in the axial direction — a one-quad-tall cylinder band
+/// between two fillet tori, common in a dense fillet network — the vertex
+/// residual barely constrains the axis, and a least-squares cone will happily
+/// tip its axis into the band's own plane and beat the true cylinder on
+/// residual (measured on \`stepped_block_toroidal_fillets\`: a bogus 12.2°
+/// cone at 3.8e-7 mm against the correct r = 0.5 cylinder at 3.9e-6 mm, with
+/// the cone's axis nearly *anti-parallel* to the facet normals). The normals
+/// are unambiguous where the positions are degenerate, so they decide.
+///
+/// Judged on the median face so a few noisy facets cannot veto a real fit;
+/// individual offenders are still filtered by \`convexity_check\` during growth.
+fn axis_normals_consistent(
+    face_list: &[usize],
+    faces: &[MeshFace],
+    axis: &[f64; 3],
+    half_angle: f64,
+) -> bool {
+    let expected = half_angle.sin().abs();
+    let mut devs: Vec<f64> = face_list
+        .iter()
+        .filter_map(|&fi| faces[fi].normal)
+        .map(|n| (dot3(&n, axis).abs() - expected).abs())
+        .collect();
+    if devs.is_empty() {
+        return true;
+    }
+    devs.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
+    devs[devs.len() / 2] <= NORMAL_AXIS_TOL
+}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    use super::*;
    use std::f64::consts::PI;

    /// Generate points on a cylinder: n_rings rings of n_pts_per_ring points.
    fn cylinder_points(
        axis_point: [f64; 3],
        axis_dir: [f64; 3],
        radius: f64,
        n_rings: usize,
        n_pts_per_ring: usize,
        h_min: f64,
        h_max: f64,
    ) -> Vec<MeshVertex> {
        let d = {
            let len = (axis_dir[0].powi(2) + axis_dir[1].powi(2) + axis_dir[2].powi(2)).sqrt();
            [axis_dir[0] / len, axis_dir[1] / len, axis_dir[2] / len]
        };
        let (u, w) = super::super::perpendicular_basis(&d);
        let mut pts = Vec::new();
        for ring in 0..n_rings {
            let t = if n_rings == 1 { 0.5 } else { ring as f64 / (n_rings - 1) as f64 };
            let h = h_min + t * (h_max - h_min);
            for j in 0..n_pts_per_ring {
                let theta = 2.0 * PI * j as f64 / n_pts_per_ring as f64;
                let (sin_t, cos_t) = theta.sin_cos();
                pts.push(MeshVertex::from_xyz(
                    axis_point[0] + h * d[0] + radius * (cos_t * u[0] + sin_t * w[0]),
                    axis_point[1] + h * d[1] + radius * (cos_t * u[1] + sin_t * w[1]),
                    axis_point[2] + h * d[2] + radius * (cos_t * u[2] + sin_t * w[2]),
                ));
            }
        }
        pts
    }

    /// Generate face normals for a cylinder (radially outward).
    fn cylinder_normals(axis_dir: [f64; 3], n_faces: usize) -> Vec<[f64; 3]> {
        let d = {
            let len = (axis_dir[0].powi(2) + axis_dir[1].powi(2) + axis_dir[2].powi(2)).sqrt();
            [axis_dir[0] / len, axis_dir[1] / len, axis_dir[2] / len]
        };
        let (u, w) = super::super::perpendicular_basis(&d);
        (0..n_faces)
            .map(|i| {
                let theta = 2.0 * PI * i as f64 / n_faces as f64;
                let (sin_t, cos_t) = theta.sin_cos();
                [cos_t * u[0] + sin_t * w[0],
                 cos_t * u[1] + sin_t * w[1],
                 cos_t * u[2] + sin_t * w[2]]
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// Build a synthetic cylinder mesh suitable for fit_cylinder.
    /// Returns (faces, vertices) where faces have normals and vertex_indices set.
    fn build_cylinder_mesh(
        axis_point: [f64; 3],
        axis_dir: [f64; 3],
        radius: f64,
        n_rings: usize,
        n_pts_per_ring: usize,
        h_min: f64,
        h_max: f64,
    ) -> (Vec<MeshFace>, Vec<MeshVertex>) {
        let vertices = cylinder_points(axis_point, axis_dir, radius, n_rings, n_pts_per_ring, h_min, h_max);
        let normals = cylinder_normals(axis_dir, n_rings * n_pts_per_ring);
        // Create one face per vertex (using adjacent vertices as a triangle)
        let mut faces = Vec::new();
        for ring in 0..n_rings.saturating_sub(1) {
            for j in 0..n_pts_per_ring {
                let j_next = (j + 1) % n_pts_per_ring;
                let i0 = ring * n_pts_per_ring + j;
                let i1 = ring * n_pts_per_ring + j_next;
                let i2 = (ring + 1) * n_pts_per_ring + j;
                let fidx = faces.len();
                faces.push(MeshFace {
                    vertex_count: 3,
                    vertex_indices: [i0, i1, i2, 0],
                    neighbors: [-1, -1, -1, -1],
                    normal: Some(normals[fidx % normals.len()]),
                });
            }
        }
        (faces, vertices)
    }

=== competition tests
//! Integration tests for stage 2.3(b) scoped fit competition: tangent-chain
//! regions the whole-region ladder cannot explain must decompose into their
//! true analytic surfaces (vertex-tolerance validated, not just counted).
//!
//! These run the full stage-2 pipeline (default stage) and assert the typed
//! hypothesis counts on the headline acceptance models, including the
//! stage-2.3(c) bent-tube promotion win (pipe elbow → torus + 2 cylinders).

use brepper::config;
use brepper::{stage1, stage2};

fn manifest_dir() -> String {
    env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").to_string()
}

fn run(stl_rel: &str) -> stage2::Stage2Output {
    let stl = format!("{}/{stl_rel}", manifest_dir());
    let config = config::parse_config_from(["brepper", &stl, "-q"]).unwrap();
    let mesh = stage1::stage1(&config).expect("stage1");
    stage2::stage2(&config, mesh, None).expect("stage2")
}

/// Every mesh face is covered by exactly one selected surface.
fn assert_total_coverage(out: &stage2::Stage2Output) {
    let n = out.mesh.faces.len();
    let mut count = vec![0u32; n];
    for s in &out.selected_surfaces {
        let faces = match s {
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Planar(i) => &out.planar_hypotheses[*i].faces,
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Conical(i) => &out.conical_hypotheses[*i].faces,
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Spherical(i) => &out.spherical_hypotheses[*i].faces,
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Toroidal(i) => &out.toroidal_hypotheses[*i].faces,
            stage2::SelectedSurface::BSpline(i) => &out.bspline_hypotheses[*i].faces,
        };
        for &fi in faces {
            count[fi] += 1;
        }
    }
    assert!(count.iter().all(|&c| c == 1), "every face covered exactly once");
}

#[test]
fn competition_rounded_cube_shell_decomposes_6_12_8() {
    // The rounded-cube outer shell is one smooth region (a tangent chain);
    // competition must split it into 6 planes + 12 fillet cylinders + 8
    // corner spheres — the reference's 26 analytic faces.
    let out = run("tests/onshape/rounded_cube_10_r2_fine.stl");
    let cylinders = out.conical_hypotheses.iter().filter(|h| h.is_cylinder()).count();
    let cones = out.conical_hypotheses.iter().filter(|h| !h.is_cylinder()).count();
    assert_eq!(out.spherical_hypotheses.len(), 8, "8 corner spheres");
    assert_eq!(cylinders, 12, "12 edge-fillet cylinders");
    assert_eq!(cones, 0, "no cones");
    assert_eq!(out.planar_hypotheses.len(), 6, "6 face planes");
    assert_eq!(out.selected_surfaces.len(), 26, "26 analytic surfaces total");
    assert_total_coverage(&out);
}

    /// axis tipped into the surface — the degeneracy a thin, one-quad-tall band
    /// leaves in the vertex residual (`axis_normals_consistent`).
    #[test]
    fn axis_normals_reject_axis_tipped_into_the_surface() {

fn competition_pipe_elbow_torus_two_cylinders() {
    // The pipe elbow is one smooth tangent chain: two straight tube segments
    // joined by a 90° bend, capped by two end disks. Stage 2.3(c) bent-tube
    // promotion must recognize the bend as a torus, so competition + the
    // ladder yield 1 torus + 2 cylinders + 2 base planes = 5 surfaces (the
    // reference's 5 analytic faces), with no strip machinery and no
    // per-facet leftovers.
    let out = run("tests/onshape/pipe_elbow_10_medium.stl");
    assert_eq!(out.toroidal_hypotheses.len(), 1, "1 bend torus");
    let cylinders = out.conical_hypotheses.iter().filter(|h| h.is_cylinder()).count();
    let cones = out.conical_hypotheses.iter().filter(|h| !h.is_cylinder()).count();
    assert_eq!(cylinders, 2, "2 straight tube cylinders");
    assert_eq!(cones, 0, "no cones");
    assert_eq!(out.planar_hypotheses.len(), 2, "2 end-cap planes");
    assert_eq!(out.selected_surfaces.len(), 5, "torus + 2 cyl + 2 planes");
    assert_total_coverage(&out);
}

#[test]
fn competition_nosecone_cone_sphere_base() {
    // The nosecone's cone+sphere tangent chain is one region; the base disk
    // is a separate sharp-bounded plane. Competition + the ladder together
    // yield cone + sphere + base = 3 surfaces (the reference's 3 faces).
    let out = run("tests/onshape/nosecone_medium.stl");
    assert_eq!(out.spherical_hypotheses.len(), 1, "1 nose sphere");
    let cones = out.conical_hypotheses.iter().filter(|h| !h.is_cylinder()).count();
    assert_eq!(cones, 1, "1 body cone");
    assert_eq!(out.planar_hypotheses.len(), 1, "1 base plane");
    assert_eq!(out.selected_surfaces.len(), 3, "cone + sphere + base");
    assert_total_coverage(&out);
}
```

    Both now build real B-rep topology and reach stage 3.

    tori against the reference's 18 and only 7 real planes against 16, i.e.
    over-grown fillet tori are eating flat wall strips, and stage 3.1's

    Fixes that got it here, each a real bug with a measured mechanism:
    (a) **degenerate cone on a thin support** (`axis_normals_consistent`,
    conical.rs). An r = 0.5 fillet band one quad tall between two corner tori
    leaves the axis barely constrained by the vertex residual, so the
    least-squares cone tips its axis *into the band's own plane* and beats the
    true cylinder: a bogus 12.2° cone at 3.8e-7 mm against the correct
    r = 0.5003 cylinder at 3.9e-6 mm, its axis nearly anti-parallel to the
    facet normals. `convexity_check` then rejected every face of that fit, so
    the seed grew nothing and the whole band fell through to the leftover
    blob. The facet normals are unambiguous exactly where the positions are
    degenerate (on a cone `|n·axis| = sin(half_angle)` identically), so the
    fit is now accepted only if its own support's *median* facet agrees.
    (b) **seed patch bounded in space, not just in hops** (`PATCH_RADII`,
    compete.rs). `MAX_PATCH_DEPTH` = 3 hops walks ~18 mm along a fillet chain
    swept with 6 mm facets, straddling several segments; the patch is now also
    capped at 4 radii of curvature of the seed's own jet (flats unbounded).
    Ablation: without it the medium mesh collapses back to 2615 per-facet
    planes. `condition_patch` also shrinks toward the seed when the patch
    admits no fit at all, instead of giving up with nothing to rank by.
    (c) **freeform fitted a disconnected face set** (bspline.rs). When the
    small analytic islands are *not* absorbed, stage 2.3(e) was fitting the
    leftover faces alone — which the islands may have been the only thing
    connecting. `build_region` then produced a region whose boundary loops
    bound different pieces, and `cut_region_seam` failed with `closed band: no
    path between boundary loops` (visible on stepped_block, part_rounded_cube
    and bspline_wave). Each leftover piece is now fitted separately; and when
    the islands split the leftovers into pieces that are each patch-sized, the
    islands are the accident and get absorbed. The freeform domain also now
    admits only *enclosed* islands — one bordering a surface competition
    explained at scale is a real small feature, not an accident adrift in
    freeform — which is what stops a densely-filleted model pulling its whole
    decomposition into one nonsensical freeform domain.

# Instructions for LLM Coding Assistants

This file contains guidelines for AI/LLM coding assistants working on this project. Read ALL of AGENTS.md - no just the first 100 lines.

The shell is zsh. Use zsh quoting conventions. "echo ===" will fail, and globs in flags must be quoted.

### Commit Checklist (MANDATORY — verify before every commit)

- \`cargo clippy\` emits no warnings.
- Build passes with no errors or warnings.

## Project Layout

This is a Rust project. Key locations:

- \`README.md\` - Program usage. Read it.
- \`DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md\` - Development plan. Read it.
- \`Cargo.toml\` — Rust project manifest
- \`src/\` — Rust source files
  - \`bin/brepper.rs\` — the main program
  - \`bin/step_measure_tolerance.rs\` — utility to measure distances from STL to correpsonding STEP
  - \`bin/viewer.rs\` — GUI to visualize STL or STEP files
- \`scripts/\` — shell scripts for batch operations over test data
  - \`step_distance_table.sh\` - runs \`step_measure_tolerance\` over all STL/STEP pairs and summarizes statistics
- \`tests/\` — STL and STEP test file pairs
  - \`manual/\` — handcrafted simple models
  - \`onshape/\` — models exported from Onshape
  - \`ccad/generated/\` — models generated via CodeCAD

### OCCT / opencascade-rs

The project uses the \`opencascade-sys\` crate (auto-generated Rust FFI bindings to OpenCASCADE Technology) via a path dependency. MANDATORY: All useful C++ OCCT APIs should be available in the binding - if you want to use one that doesn't seem to be bound, complain loudly about it AND STOP.

\`\`\`

../opencascade-rs/crates/occt-sys/OCCT/src/  ← OCCT C++ source (for reading docs/headers)
../opencascade-rs/crates/occt-sys/OCCT/dox/  ← OCCT C++ documentation
\`\`\`

The \`builtin\` feature (default) compiles OCCT from source — first build takes ~8 minutes. Subsequent builds are fast.

## Commit Messages

All commit messages must include:

1. **A clear description** of the changes made

3. **The user prompts** that led to the changes

Done. Summary of the session:

## What I found

The `stepped_block_toroidal` blocker was **three separate bugs**, and the inherited diagnosis was wrong on a key point: competition was *not* committing 0 analytic surfaces — it committed 100 hypotheses and left only 138 of 2615 faces unexplained. The `LEFTOVER_BLOB_MAX` whole-region discard in [classify.rs](src/stage2/classify.rs:189) then threw the whole thing away.

**1. A degenerate cone beat the true cylinder.** An r = 0.5 fillet band *one quad tall* between two corner tori leaves the axis barely constrained by the vertex residual, so the least-squares cone tips its axis into the band's own plane — a bogus 12.2° cone at 3.8e-7 mm against the correct r = 0.5003 cylinder at 3.9e-6 mm, its axis nearly *anti-parallel* to the facet normals. `fit_surface` picks by residual, so the cone won; `convexity_check` then rejected every face of it, the seed grew nothing, and the band became the leftover blob. On a cone `|n·axis| = sin(half_angle)` holds identically, so the normals pin the axis exactly where the positions are degenerate — a fit is now accepted only if its own support's median facet agrees.

**2. The seed patch was bounded in hops, not in space.** Three BFS hops walk ~18 mm along a fillet chain swept with 6 mm facets, straddling several segments. Now also capped at 4 curvature radii of the seed's jet. Ablation-verified load-bearing: removing it collapses the medium mesh again.

**3. `closed band: no path between boundary loops` — fully explained.** Freeform was fitting the leftover faces alone when the small analytic islands weren't absorbed, but the islands were sometimes the only thing connecting those faces. `build_region` produced loops bounding different pieces, so the seam search legitimately found no path. Each piece is now fitted separately, plus two related corrections to the absorb rule.

## Results

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| fine (26122 faces) | 26122 per-facet planes | **74 analytic surfaces** (ref: 71) |
| medium (2615 faces) | 2615 per-facet planes | **124 surfaces** |

Both now reach stage 3 with real B-rep topology. Suite: **499 passing, 4 ignored, clippy clean** (was 498/4) — no regressions. Committed as `2fcf888` with new guards in `conical.rs` and `tests/stage2_competition.rs`.

## What's still open

The two stage-4 `--compare` tests stay disabled, but the blocker has changed character — it's now **exactness**, not collapse. Fine commits 24 tori against the reference's 18 and only 7 real planes against 16: over-grown fillet tori are eating flat wall strips, leaving stage 3.1's reference-edge compare 4.4e-2 mm out (2.1e-1 mm on medium). That's the natural next target, and it's recorded with measurements in TODO.md.

use brepper::config;

use brepper::stage2::edges::{classify_edges, compute_jet_field, EdgeClass};
use brepper::stage2::regions::extract_regions;
use brepper::stage1;

fn centroid(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize) -> [f64; 3] {
    let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
    let vc = f.vertex_count as usize;
    let mut c = [0.0; 3];
    for &vi in &f.vertex_indices[..vc] {
        let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
        c[0] += v.x;
        c[1] += v.y;
        c[2] += v.z;
    }
    let n = vc as f64;
    [c[0] / n, c[1] / n, c[2] / n]
}

"""/// Area of a mesh face (triangle, or a quad as two triangles).
fn tri_area(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize) -> f64 {
    let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
    let p = |k: usize| {
        let v = &mesh.vertices[f.vertex_indices[k]];
        [v.x, v.y, v.z]
    };
    let tri = |a: [f64; 3], b: [f64; 3], c: [f64; 3]| {
        let u = [b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1], b[2] - a[2]];
        let w = [c[0] - a[0], c[1] - a[1], c[2] - a[2]];
        let x = [u[1] * w[2] - u[2] * w[1], u[2] * w[0] - u[0] * w[2], u[0] * w[1] - u[1] * w[0]];
        0.5 * (x[0] * x[0] + x[1] * x[1] + x[2] * x[2]).sqrt()
    };
    let mut a = tri(p(0), p(1), p(2));
    if f.vertex_count == 4 {
        a += tri(p(0), p(2), p(3));
    }
    a
}

fn main() {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();""")
open(p,'w').write(s)

**After:**
```
/// The radius of curvature `radius_plausible` bounds. Planes are flat and tori
/// are guarded in `torus_candidate`, so both report 0 (always plausible).
fn hyp_radius(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &CompeteHyp) -> f64 {
    match hyp {
        CompeteHyp::Conical(h) => conical_local_radius(mesh, h),
        CompeteHyp::Spherical(h) => h.radius,
        CompeteHyp::Toroidal(h) => h.major_radius,
        CompeteHyp::Planar(_) => 0.0,
    }
}

/// Is this candidate only a degenerate re-parameterization of a simpler
/// surface — one whose *own support* the simpler surface already explains?
///
/// Each analytic type contains the next simpler one as a limit: a torus with
/// R → ∞ is a cylinder, a cylinder with r → ∞ is a plane. Near that limit the
/// extra parameter is unconstrained by the data, so the richer fit matches
/// just as well and then wins the area contest by flooding a row or two
/// further — past the very junction the simpler surface stops at. The
/// bounding-box bound in `radius_plausible` only catches the gross cases; it
/// is measured against the whole model, and on a 100 mm extrusion whose
/// cross-section features are 0.5–3 mm across, an R = 114 mm "torus" over one
/// r = 1 fillet band sails under a 122 mm bar. (Ten such surfaces on
/// `stepped_block_toroidal_fillets` fine: six near-cylindrical tori eating
/// perimeter fillets, four near-planar cylinders eating flat wall strips.)
///
/// So ask the question directly instead of bounding a radius: fit the
/// degenerate limit to the candidate's own faces and see whether it validates
/// them all, at the same tolerances the candidate itself was grown at. If it
/// does, the candidate explains nothing extra and the ladder's simplest-first
/// rule rejects it — the same principle `classify_regions` applies to a whole
/// region and `resolve_claims` applies to a contested face, here applied to a
/// competition candidate. Returns the name of the simpler surface.
///
/// Only true degenerate *limits* are tested, not every lower-DOF type: a
/// sphere and a cylinder are vertex-ambiguous on a short ring-tessellated hole
/// without either being a limit of the other, and that ambiguity is settled by
/// the jet-informed rung order in `classify.rs`, not here.
fn degenerate_limit(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    hyp: &CompeteHyp,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm * GROW_VTOL_FACTOR;
    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
    let faces = hyp.faces();
    let plane = || explains::<PlanarSurface>(mesh, faces, centroids, vtol, stol).then_some("plane");
    match hyp {
        CompeteHyp::Planar(_) => None,
        CompeteHyp::Spherical(_) | CompeteHyp::Conical(_) => plane(),
        CompeteHyp::Toroidal(_) => plane().or_else(|| {
            explains::<ConicalSurface>(mesh, faces, centroids, vtol, stol).then_some("cylinder")
        }),
    }
}

/// Does surface type `S`, fitted to exactly these faces, validate every one of
/// them?
fn explains<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    faces: &[usize],
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    vtol: f64,
    stol: f64,
) -> bool {
    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, faces);
    let Some(mut fit) = S::fit_surface(mesh, faces, &verts, 0) else {
        return false;
    };
    S::determine_convexity(mesh, faces, &mut fit);
    faces
        .iter()
        .all(|&fi| face_validates::<S>(mesh, fi, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol))
}
```

> The underlying reason is structural: a torus with a large major radius relative to its minor radius is essentially a cylinder with a subtle bend, allowing it to extend fully across the cylinder's footprint while also creeping into adjacent regions. This creates an inherent advantage when comparing a model against its own degenerate variant—the richer model will always win or tie because it's a superset. That's why the validation hierarchy prioritizes simplicity first; the first model that passes validation wins, rather than selecting based on raw area metrics.

/// How far the support of a toroidal hypothesis sweeps around the torus's own
/// axis, in radians: the angular extent of its vertices about the axis, taken
/// as 2π minus the largest angular gap between consecutive vertices, so a patch
/// straddling the angle origin measures correctly.
fn torus_sweep(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &ToroidalHypothesis) -> f64 {
    let a = hyp.axis_direction;
    let (u, w) = super::perpendicular_basis(&a);
    let mut angles: Vec<f64> = hyp
        .vertices
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|&vi| {
            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
            let d = [
                v.x - hyp.center[0],
                v.y - hyp.center[1],
                v.z - hyp.center[2],
            ];
            let (x, y) = (
                d[0] * u[0] + d[1] * u[1] + d[2] * u[2],
                d[0] * w[0] + d[1] * w[1] + d[2] * w[2],
            );
            // A vertex on the axis has no meaningful angle.
            (x.hypot(y) > 1e-12).then(|| y.atan2(x))
        })
        .collect();
    if angles.len() < 2 {
        return 0.0;
    }
    angles.sort_by(|p, q| p.partial_cmp(q).unwrap());
    let mut gap = angles[0] + std::f64::consts::TAU - angles[angles.len() - 1];
    for pair in angles.windows(2) {
        gap = gap.max(pair[1] - pair[0]);
    }
    (std::f64::consts::TAU - gap).max(0.0)
}

/// before the major radius counts as determined by the data.

/// angle origin measures correctly.
///
/// This is the observable that says whether a rotational parameter is
/// determined by the data at all. A surface of revolution fitted to a patch
/// that never goes around its axis has its radius free, and a free parameter is
/// worse than useless in competition: the fit becomes a super-model of the
/// simpler surface it should have lost to — covering everything that surface
/// covers, then flooding a little further on the slack — so it takes the
/// largest-validated-area contest every time. See `MIN_TORUS_SWEEP_DEG` and
/// `MIN_CYLINDER_SWEEP_DEG`.
fn axial_sweep(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    verts: &[usize],
    origin: &[f64; 3],
    axis: &[f64; 3],
) -> f64 {
    let (u, w) = super::perpendicular_basis(axis);
    let mut angles: Vec<f64> = verts
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|&vi| {
            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
            let d = [v.x - origin[0], v.y - origin[1], v.z - origin[2]];
            let (x, y) = (
                d[0] * u[0] + d[1] * u[1] + d[2] * u[2],
                d[0] * w[0] + d[1] * w[1] + d[2] * w[2],
            );
            // A vertex on the axis has no meaningful angle.
            (x.hypot(y) > 1e-12).then(|| y.atan2(x))
        })
        .collect();
    if angles.len() < 2 {
        return 0.0;
    }
    angles.sort_by(|p, q| p.partial_cmp(q).unwrap());
    let mut gap = angles[0] + std::f64::consts::TAU - angles[angles.len() - 1];
    for pair in angles.windows(2) {
        gap = gap.max(pair[1] - pair[0]);
    }
    (std::f64::consts::TAU - gap).max(0.0)
}

fn torus_sweep(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &ToroidalHypothesis) -> f64 {
    axial_sweep(mesh, &hyp.vertices, &hyp.center, &hyp.axis_direction)

    if !hyp.is_cylinder() {
        return std::f64::consts::TAU;
    }
    axial_sweep(mesh, &hyp.vertices, &hyp.apex, &hyp.axis_direction)

## What the over-growth actually was

The 24-tori/7-planes symptom wasn't fillets "eating" walls in any ordinary sense. Ten committed surfaces were **degenerate super-models of the surface they displaced**:

- 4 near-planar cylinders on flat wall strips, r = 20, 30, 47, 116 mm

All ten passed the existing bounding-box radius bound, because that bar (121.67 mm) is set by the 100 mm extrusion length and says nothing about 0.5–3 mm cross-section features.

The mechanism generalizes: each analytic type contains the next simpler one as a limit (torus R→∞ *is* a cylinder; cylinder r→∞ *is* a plane). A patch sweeping a few degrees about its own axis never observes the revolution, so its radius is free — and a free parameter yields a **winning** fit, not a useless one. The richer model covers everything the simpler surface covers, then floods one more tessellation row past the tangent junction on the slack, taking the largest-area contest every time.

`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG = 20` rejects those. The populations don't overlap anywhere near it: real tori sweep 84.7°–103.4° (fitting R to the reference's exact 2.0000/2.5000/14.0000), impostors 3.1°–6.7°; real cylinders ≥ 64.8°, impostors 2.8°–2.9°. Cones are exempt — an apex pins the axis regardless.

## Result

Fine now commits **37 cylinders and 18 tori — the reference's counts exactly** — plus 17 planes against its 16. 72 surfaces against 71; the extra is one 0.253 mm² junction sliver. Suite 499 passing, 4 ignored, clippy clean, stage 2.3 still ~13 s.

## The `--compare` tests are still disabled, and here's why

I traced the failure to the end rather than leaving it as "not exact". It is no longer about surface choice:

1. The end-cap plane's grow swallows the first tessellation row of its fillet (9.5e-4 mm off — *under* the 1.5e-3 mm flood tolerance).
2. That drags the plane 4.7e-4 mm off true, and contaminates the fillet cylinder the same way (r = 1.0009).
3. Stage 2.4's relabel should hand the row back, but the two contaminated fits sit 3.2e-4 vs 4.7e-4 — inside its 2× anti-flapping margin.
4. The plane↔torus junction is then not classified tangent (the boundary sits one row in, where the torus normal has already turned ~2.5°).
5. So the compare applies its strict bar instead of the chordal one it reserves for tangent edges — **and that bar is unachievable in principle there**: a plane offset δ moves its intersection with a torus it should graze by √(2rδ), so a 5e-5 mm edge would need the plane fitted to ~1e-9 mm.

Three things I tried that measurably do **not** work, recorded so they aren't retried: a "does a simpler type explain this candidate's own faces" test (never fires once the sweep guard exists — deleted), a post-grow tightening pass at the strict vertex tolerance (115 of 116 grows lose their own start face; fits are only ~1e-4 mm accurate), and raising the merge size cap. The two live leads are refitting *inside* the relabel loop, and a growth tolerance that scales with facet size — one row past a tangent junction departs by ~h²/2r, so a fixed absolute bar is always too loose at fine tessellation.

This is essentially iteratively reweighted least squares. I could also try leave-one-out refitting where I compare distances against fits that exclude the boundary faces being considered, though that's expensive. The simplest defensible approach might be to iterate by refitting each surface on its current support while making relabel decisions against fits that exclude the boundary faces under consideration. This is really just alternating optimization like k-means: fit surfaces, reassign boundary faces to their best match, repeat. The current code only refits once at the end and uses a 2× margin to prevent oscillation, but that margin blocks reassignment when the fits are contaminated. //! Stage 2.4: resolution & repair.
//!
//! Turns stage 2.3's per-region hypotheses into a strict, connected,
//! validated partition. All operations are fit-validated and deterministic
//! (fixed iteration order — by surface index, smallest first for merges —
//! bounded rounds).
//!
//! - **Boundary relabel** (±1-row polish): move a region-boundary face to an
//!   adjacent surface that fits its vertices at least 2× better. Region
//!   geometry is not refitted — only the membership map changes. Iterates to
//!   a fixpoint (≤ 10 rounds; boundaries only move locally).
//! - **Merge**: absorb a small region S into an adjacent, larger, real
//!   surface T when every vertex of S lies within \`--vertex-tolerance\` of T's
//!   fitted surface and every centroid within \`--surface-tolerance\`; refit
//!   the union, revalidate, keep only if valid. Eats junction-circle
//!   singletons and chord-degenerate slivers with a principled criterion —
//!   vertex tolerance, at which "on the same surface" is decisive.
//! - **Connectivity re-split**: relabel/merge can disconnect a surface;
//!   re-split into mesh-connected components (identical fitted geometry on
//!   two non-adjacent regions is legal).
//! - **Invariants** (hard checks before stage 3): total coverage and
//!   per-surface mesh connectivity.
//!

/// Sorted, deduplicated vertex indices of a face set.
fn vertices_of(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize]) -> Vec<usize> {
    let mut v: Vec<usize> = faces
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|&fi| {

            mesh.faces[fi].vertex_indices[..vc].iter().copied()
        })
        .collect();
    v.sort_unstable();
    v.dedup();
    v
}

/// Refit a surface's geometry to its current face set, in place, keeping the

fn refit_geometry(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, cls: &mut Classification, si: usize) {
    let faces = surface_faces(cls, si).to_vec();
    if faces.is_empty() {
        return;
    }

/// Refit a committed hypothesis to its current face set, keeping the existing
/// fit if the fitter cannot produce one.
fn refit_in_place(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &mut CompeteHyp, config: &Config) {
    let faces = hyp.faces().to_vec();
    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &faces);
    let v = config.verbosity;
    match hyp {
        CompeteHyp::Planar(h) => {
            if let Some(fit) = PlanarSurface::fit_surface(mesh, &faces, &verts, v) {
                *h = PlanarSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces, verts, &fit);
            }
        }
        CompeteHyp::Conical(h) => {
            if let Some(mut fit) = ConicalSurface::fit_surface(mesh, &faces, &verts, v) {

                *h = ConicalSurface::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces, verts, &fit);
            }
        }

        }
    }
}

            let fi: Vec<usize> = (0..faces.len()).collect();
            let vs: Vec<usize> = (0..vertices.len()).collect();
            let (origin, dir, radius) = fit_cylinder(&fi, &vs, &faces, &vertices)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{nrows}x{ncols} arc should fit a cylinder"));
            assert!(
                (radius - r).abs() < 1e-9,
                "{nrows}x{ncols}: radius should be {r}, got {radius}"
            );
            assert!(
                dir[1].abs() > 1.0 - 1e-9,
                "{nrows}x{ncols}: axis should be along Y, got {dir:?}"
            );
            let worst = vs
                .iter()
                .map(|&v| vertex_to_cylinder_distance(&vertices[v], &origin, &dir, radius).abs())
                .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
            assert!(worst < 1e-9, "{nrows}x{ncols}: worst vertex residual {worst:.3e}");
        }
    }

'''

open(p,'w').write(s)

Committed. **`stepped_block_toroidal` fine now passes the full `--compare`.**

## Refitting inside the relabel loop closed it — but not on its own

Your lead was right, and it needed one thing in front of it. Relabel was making **zero** moves on this model, so there was nothing to iterate. The reason: `fit_plane` area-weights its *normal* but took a plain **vertex mean** for the *offset*. The end cap is a few large flat quads ringed by the many tiny quads of its fillet's first row — ~1% of the area but half the vertices — so the plane sat at the **midpoint** of the two levels. Every one of its 95 faces was 4.7e-4 mm out with a *flat* residual distribution and no outlier group for relabel to see. Area-weighting is independently just the correct discretization of ∫(n·x−d)²dA.

With that, relabel went 0 → 81 moves. Adding the refit inside the loop took it to 105 and the surface count from 73 to exactly 71.

## The bigger find

Chasing a leftover 3.5e-2 mm vertex error turned up that fits were **stale** in two places — a fit is only a statement about the faces it was computed from, and the faces a later step removes are exactly the junction rows that pulled it off true:

- `resolve_claims` trims a hypothesis to the faces it won but kept the fit from everything its flood reached.
- `relabel_boundaries` iterated ten rounds rebuilding only face *lists* — `rebuild_all` never refits.

This was corpus-wide, not specific to this model. `rounded_cube`'s r=2 fillets read **1.9976–1.9984 with no vertex closer than 5e-4 mm** to their own surface, on a mesh whose vertices are 1.9e-6 mm from the true CAD surfaces. They now read **2.0000 at 1.6e-6** — a thousandfold, on a model whose tests were already passing.

I suspected the fitter first and it was innocent: `cylinder_fit_exact_on_partial_arc` now pins that down (a single row of quads across 90° recovers r to 1e-9).

The amplification explains the original symptom: a plane offset δ moves its intersection with a torus it should *graze* by √(2rδ), so 4.7e-4 mm of plane error became the 4.4e-2 mm edge error.

## Status

Suite **502 passing, 3 ignored** (was 499/4), clippy clean.

Medium stays disabled, but it's a different problem now — coarse sampling, not accuracy. Its tori are still exactly 18, cylinders 38 vs 37, every plane fits to ~1e-14; but the r=0.5/r=1 fillets near the end caps have too few facets and ~24 stay per-facet (96 surfaces vs 71). The lead is a growth tolerance that scales with facet size: one row past a tangent junction departs by ~h²/2r, so a fixed absolute bar is simultaneously too loose at fine tessellation and too tight at coarse.

/// initial fit: jet-similar faces (same curvature class, magnitude within 2×,
/// and within `PATCH_RADII` radii of curvature) where the jet is informative.
///
/// Falls back to the plain topological neighbourhood when that leaves too
/// little to fit. The jet is a *prior*, not a gate — validation decides every
/// face — and on a small fillet tessellated into a handful of facets it is
/// simply not reliable enough to gate on: measured on
/// `stepped_block_toroidal_fillets` medium, adjacent facets of one exact
/// r = 0.5 arc read κ₁ = 0.023, 0.162 and 2.2 (radii of 43 mm, 6 mm and
/// 0.45 mm for the same 0.5 mm fillet). The similarity filter then admits 2–4
/// faces, too few to determine a 5-DOF cylinder, so every candidate fails and
/// the arc degrades to one plane per facet. Handing the fit an unfiltered
/// neighbourhood instead costs nothing in soundness: a patch straddling a
/// junction is what `condition_patch` trims and what flood validation rejects.
fn seed_patch(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, in_region: &[bool], seed: usize, jet: &[JetField]) -> Vec<usize> {
    let patch = grow_patch(mesh, in_region, seed, jet, true);
    if patch.len() >= MIN_CONDITION_FACES {
        return patch;
    }
    grow_patch(mesh, in_region, seed, jet, false)
}

/// Depth-limited BFS around `seed`, optionally filtered by jet similarity.
fn grow_patch(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    seed: usize,
    jet: &[JetField],
    use_jet: bool,
) -> Vec<usize> {
    let seed_class = curvature_class(jet[seed]);
    let seed_mag = jet[seed].k1.abs().max(jet[seed].k2.abs());
    let seed_c = super::face_centroid(&mesh.faces[seed], &mesh.vertices);
    let radius_limit = if use_jet && seed_mag > 1e-9 {
        PATCH_RADII / seed_mag
    } else {
        f64::INFINITY
    };
    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
    seen.insert(seed);
    let mut out = vec![seed];
    // Depth-limited BFS (frontier by ring).
    let mut frontier = vec![seed];
    for _depth in 0..MAX_PATCH_DEPTH {
        if out.len() >= SEED_PATCH_CAP {
            break;
        }
        let mut next = Vec::new();
        for &fi in &frontier {
            let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
            for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
                if ni < 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                let ni = ni as usize;
                if !in_region[ni] || seen.contains(&ni) {
                    continue;
                }
                if use_jet {
                    if curvature_class(jet[ni]) != seed_class {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let mag = jet[ni].k1.abs().max(jet[ni].k2.abs());
                    if seed_mag > 1e-9 && (mag > 1.5 * seed_mag || mag < 0.667 * seed_mag) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let c = super::face_centroid(&mesh.faces[ni], &mesh.vertices);
                    let d = ((c[0] - seed_c[0]).powi(2)
                        + (c[1] - seed_c[1]).powi(2)
                        + (c[2] - seed_c[2]).powi(2))
                    .sqrt();
                    if d > radius_limit {
                        continue;
                    }
                }
                seen.insert(ni);
                out.push(ni);
                next.push(ni);
                if out.len() >= SEED_PATCH_CAP {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        frontier = next;
    }
    out.sort_unstable();
    out
}

'''

<!-- msg_011CdShm7dWwfGDmnFTPDfXx -->

Followed it, and it went somewhere — just not where the lead pointed.

## The lead is refuted

Scaling the growth tolerance with facet size doesn't work. On medium, `GROW_VTOL_FACTOR` ×1 gives 112 surfaces, **×3.3 collapses the whole model to 2615 per-facet planes**, ×10 gives 90 with a spurious sphere and a 19th torus. Not monotonic, not a matter of degree — loosening doesn't recover coarse fillets, it just changes which accidents win.

## What actually starves them

`seed_patch` was **gating** its BFS on jet similarity. On a small fillet tessellated into a handful of facets the jet is not fit to gate on: adjacent facets of one *exact* r=0.5 arc read κ₁ = 0.023, 0.162 and 2.2 — radii of 43 mm, 6 mm and 0.45 mm for the same 0.5 mm fillet. The filter admitted 2–4 faces, far too few for a 5-DOF cylinder, so every candidate failed and the arc became one plane per facet.

Stage 2.3(b) already says the jet *only orders and prunes* and validation decides every face — the code just wasn't holding to it. It now falls back to the plain topological neighbourhood when the filtered patch is too small to fit. Nothing is risked: a straddling patch is exactly what `condition_patch` trims and flood validation rejects.

Medium: **96 → 82 surfaces** (reference 71), compare 2.1e-1 → 1.6e-1 mm, tori already exactly 18. Fine unchanged and still passing.

## The more useful finding

I walked into the real blocker repeatedly: **`LEFTOVER_BLOB_MAX`'s whole-region discard is a cliff.** Medium sits at largest-blob 5 of 8, and *every* knob I tried — growth tolerance ×3.3, `MIN_CONDITION_FACES` 6→4, `PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS` 16→32, capping the fallback patch at 8/10/14 — pushes it over 8 and nukes all 2615 faces to per-facet.

That has a nasty second-order effect worth flagging: several constants *look* load-bearing at their current values when they are only on the safe side of the cliff. No incremental improvement on coarse meshes can be measured while a local defect triggers a global catastrophe. The discard earned its place (rounded_cube coarse: 43 BRepCheck failures → 0), so it shouldn't be deleted — made proportionate, scoped to the offending neighbourhood or gated on blob size *relative* to the region, with stage-3/4 validity measured directly since that's what it protects.

## Also

`competition_stepped_block_fillet_network_stays_analytic` was counting raw hypotheses — repair can empty one without removing it from its vector, so it read 38 cylinders where the reconstruction has 37. Fixed to count *selected* surfaces per project policy; it now pins the exact reference decomposition (37 + 18 + 16 = 71).

Suite: 502 passing, 3 ignored, clippy clean. Committed.

fn residual_scale<S: SurfaceType>(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize], fit: &S::Fit) -> f64 {

+/// Robust scale of a fit's own residuals over its support: the median distance
+/// from a support vertex to the fitted surface.
+///
+/// The *median*, not the RMS, because the faces this scale exists to detect are
+/// sitting in the sample. A support of 85 true faces plus 10 leaked junction
+/// rows at 9.5e-4 mm has an RMS of 3.1e-4 — inflated by the very outliers it is
+/// meant to expose, and enough to keep admitting them — while its median stays
+/// at the true faces' ~1e-6.
+fn residual_scale<S: SurfaceType>(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, faces: &[usize], fit: &S::Fit) -> f64 {
+    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, faces);
+    if verts.is_empty() {
+        return 0.0;
+    }
+    let mut d: Vec<f64> = verts
+        .iter()
+        .map(|&vi| {
+            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
+            S::vertex_distance(fit, &[v.x, v.y, v.z])
+        })
+        .collect();
+    d.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
+    d[d.len() / 2]
+}

fn competition_rounded_cube_shell_decomposes_6_12_8() {
    // The rounded-cube outer shell is one smooth region (a tangent chain);
    // competition must split it into 6 planes + 12 fillet cylinders + 8
    // corner spheres — the reference's 26 analytic faces.
    let out = run("tests/onshape/rounded_cube_10_r2_fine.stl");

cat > tmp/COMMITMSG <<'EOF'
Calibrate flood acceptance on each fit's own residuals, not a constant

Whether a face belongs to a surface was decided at a fixed bar,
`GROW_VTOL_FACTOR` × `--vertex-tolerance` = 1.5e-3 mm. A single absolute
tolerance cannot be right here, because it has to be loose enough for the
worst-conditioned fit in the corpus and is then hundreds of times too loose for
a converged one — which is exactly how the end-cap plane of
stepped_block_toroidal fine came to swallow the first row of its perimeter
fillet.

The two quantities being compared are not the same kind of thing. A mesh vertex
lies on the true CAD surface to ~1e-6 mm — measured, and on coarse tessellations
too (rounded_cube fine 1.9e-6, stepped_block fine 1.2e-5) — so a face that
really belongs to a surface misses its fit by the *fit's* error and nothing
else, while a face that does not belong misses it by a geometric departure: one
tessellation row past a tangent junction sits ~h²/2r away, shrinking
quadratically as the mesh refines. The gap is enormous and no fixed bar can
straddle it: the row that used to be swallowed was 9.5e-4 mm from a fit accurate
to 1e-6, some 950× the fit's own scale, where a genuine face sits at 1.

`acceptance_tol` (compete.rs) therefore scales the bar by the fit's own robust
residual scale. A fit still bootstrapping off a partial patch reports a large
scale and keeps the room it needs to grow; the bar tightens by itself as the
support fills in and the fit converges. The scale is a *median*, not an RMS,
because the faces it exists to detect are sitting in the sample — a support of
85 true faces plus 10 leaked rows at 9.5e-4 mm has an RMS of 3.1e-4, inflated by
the very outliers it should expose and still loose enough to keep admitting
them, while its median stays at the true faces' ~1e-6.

Two properties are the point. The criterion carries no length, so it needs no
recalibration per model, feature size or tessellation density. And it is
insensitive to its own parameter: the corpus decomposes identically at 5, 8 and
15 σ, where the absolute bar it replaces went from correct to total collapse
over a 3.3× change.

Honest accounting: this did **not** remove a constant. `GROW_VTOL_FACTOR` is
demoted from operative value to a safety ceiling and `RESIDUAL_SIGMAS` takes its
place, so the count is unchanged. The ceiling is load-bearing, for the reason a
self-calibrating criterion always needs one — a poor fit reports a large scale,
admits more foreign faces and inflates its scale further. Measured: removing it
costs bspline_wave its single freeform patch (6 surfaces → 16) and
stepped_block_toroidal fine its exact decomposition (71 → 74).

Results hold: stepped_block fine still reconstructs to exactly the reference's
71 surfaces and passes `--compare`; rounded_cube still gives 6 + 12 + 8; medium
edges from 82 surfaces to 81.

Also converts the three older competition tests to count *selected* surfaces via
the `selected_counts` helper, matching project policy and the fix already made
to the stepped_block test. Repair can empty a hypothesis without removing it
from its vector, so raw-vector counts read 8 planes on rounded_cube where the
reconstruction has 6 — a latent trap that fires whenever repair merges anything.

## 🤖 Assistant
<!-- msg_011CdTqHCwuPUqb5hbworoNF -->

Committed as `8e21a18`. Suite 502 passing, 3 ignored, clippy clean.

## What #1 changed

The flood bar now scales with each fit's **own median residual**, clamped between `--vertex-tolerance` and the old fixed bar:

```
tol = clamp(5 × median_residual(fit, its support), vtol, 30·vtol)
```

The justification is that the old comparison was between incommensurable quantities. A mesh vertex sits on the true CAD surface to ~1e-6 mm (measured, coarse tessellations included), so a face that *belongs* misses its fit by the fit's error alone; a face that *doesn't* misses by a geometric departure, ~h²/2r one row past a tangent junction. The row that used to be swallowed was 950× the fit's own scale where a genuine face sits at 1 — no single absolute bar straddles that.

Median rather than RMS, because the outliers are *in* the sample: 85 good faces plus 10 leaked rows gives an RMS of 3.1e-4, still loose enough to keep admitting them, while the median stays at 1e-6.

**The property worth having:** identical corpus decompositions at 5, 8 and 15 σ. The bar it replaces went from correct to total collapse over a 3.3× change.

## Two honest caveats

- **It did not remove a constant.** `GROW_VTOL_FACTOR` is demoted to a safety ceiling and `RESIDUAL_SIGMAS` takes its place — count unchanged. I tested removing the ceiling; it's load-bearing (wave 6→16 surfaces, stepped_block fine 71→74), which is the runaway a self-calibrating criterion always risks.
- I also found the other three competition tests counting **raw hypotheses** rather than selected surfaces — repair can empty a hypothesis without removing it from its vector, so rounded_cube read 8 planes where the reconstruction has 6. All four now use a shared `selected_counts` helper. That trap fires whenever repair merges anything.

## Next steps, now in TODO.md under "Make the stage-2 decomposition robust rather than tuned"

2. **Price model complexity instead of maximizing area.** The types nest (torus ⊃ cylinder ⊃ plane), so a richer model can always match the simpler one's area and add a bit by bending across a junction. `radius_plausible`, `MAX_TORUS_RADIUS_RATIO`, `MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG` and `MIN/MAX_HALF_ANGLE_DEG` are five guards fighting that one bias. Falsifiable: delete them, add an MDL score, see if the corpus holds.
3. **Global parameter consensus.** Every surface is fitted independently, discarding the strongest CAD prior — that features repeat. `stepped_block` has exactly four radii; we produce a cloud around each (2.9996, 3.0004, 1.0009, 1.0018). Cluster, recover shared values, refit constrained.
4. **Make the `LEFTOVER_BLOB_MAX` fallback proportionate.** The cliff that makes coarse meshes untunable. Needs stage-3 robustness at analytic/per-facet boundaries first, and validity measured directly.
5. **Snap boundaries to computed intersection curves.** Every remaining `--compare` failure is a boundary one row off, yet nothing reasons about where a boundary *should* be.
6. **A randomized sweep harness over `gen_test_models`.** Guards accumulate because the feedback loop is one hand-inspected model at a time — which is how overfitting happens.

My recommendation for next session is #2: it's the one that deletes five guards for one principle, and it's directly falsifiable against the existing corpus.
